examples.japanese: {砂|すな}の{粒度|りゅうど}を{測定|そくてい}する。
examples.english: Measure the grain size of sand.

examples.japanese: {粒度|りゅうど}の{細|こま}かい{研磨剤|けんまざい}を{使|つか}う。
この{土壌|どじょう}は{粒度|りゅうど}{分布|ぶんぷ}が{均一|きんいつ}で、{水|みず}はけがいい。
examples.english: This soil has a uniform grain size distribution and drains well.

examples.japanese: データの{粒度|りゅうど}を{上|あ}げる。
examples.english: Increase the granularity of the data.

examples.japanese: タスクの{粒度|りゅうど}が{粗|あら}すぎる。
examples.english: The task granularity is too coarse.

examples.japanese: {報告|ほうこく}の{粒度|りゅうど}を{揃|そろ}えてから{提出|ていしゅつ}してください。
examples.english: Please align the level of detail in your reports before submitting.

notes:
Originally a technical term from materials science for the size of particles or grains. Now widely used in IT, business, and project management to describe how finely something is broken down or specified.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粒度|りゅうど}が{細|こま}かい／{粗|あら}い — fine / coarse granularity
- {粒度|りゅうど}{分布|ぶんぷ} — grain size distribution
- {粒度|りゅうど}を{揃|そろ}える — to align the level of detail
- {粒度|りゅうど}{分析|ぶんせき} — grain size analysis; granularity analysis

USAGE:
In business and IT contexts, {粒度|りゅうど}が{細|こま}かい means highly detailed (fine-grained), and {粒度|りゅうど}が{粗|あら}い means broad or high-level (coarse-grained). This figurative extension is very productive in modern Japanese workplace communication.
